101	# ADR-0003: The merge to `main` is the approval gate: two people, code owners, on-call co-ownership
102	
103	- **Status:** Accepted
104	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
105	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-5, GĐ-8, GĐ-11; OD2, OD5, OD7, OD9, OD10, OD13)
106	- **Scope:** GitHub monorepo rulesets, CODEOWNERS, `production` environment, on-call schedule
107	
108	## 1. Context
109	
110	Papaya is assumed to be on GitHub Team (GĐ-5). There, environment required reviewers do not exist for private repositories (📖 R3.1.2), so
111	the deploy job cannot wait for an approval. The approval must happen earlier. Incidents need an
112	approver within 15 minutes, 24/7 (S7), and code-owner review means the approver must own the files.
113	
114	## 2. Options considered
115	
116	| Option | Pros | Cons |
117	|---|---|---|
118	| A. Upgrade to Enterprise for environment reviewers | Approval sits next to the deploy | Cost; not assumed (GĐ-5) |
119	| B. Merge to `main` as the gate; `production` limited to `main` | Works on Team; the approver sees the code that will be applied | Nobody sees the prod diff before apply (partly handled by ADR-0004) |
120	| C. More approvers for high-risk changes | More eyes | Slower; the owner wants two people per change |
121	
122	## 3. Decision
123	
124	Option B. Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
125	approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, empty
126	bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). `production` accepts only `main` (📖 R3.1.3).
127	
128	- **Two people per change:** one makes it, one approves it; the approver is always an engineer,
129	  never an agent (OD2, OD5). L3 changes need one approver too, who must own the path.
130	- **Incidents:** on-call engineers only approve; an incident responder writes the fix (OD7).
131	- **Night coverage:** an on-call approver group co-owns every deployable path in CODEOWNERS; one
132	  primary, one backup (OD9). It does not co-own process-defining paths (`.github/**`, CODEOWNERS,
133	  agent config, catalogue) or the SCP stack, which only the L3 owner team approves (OD13); IAM-only
134	  stacks are deployable, so it co-owns them with the L3 owner team.
135	- **Agent review:** an independent agent may post an automated review; it never counts as an
136	  approval (GĐ-11).
137	- **Cross-team PRs:** one approval is enough (OD10).
138	
139	## 4. Consequences
140	
141	- **Positive:** four-eyes enforced by GitHub, not by the agent. One rule for normal days and incidents.
142	- **Negative / trade-offs:** GitHub accepts an approval from any listed owner (📖 R3.2.7), so the
143	  on-call group can approve another domain's PR; domain review on normal days is a process rule.
144	  One reviewer for high-risk changes can miss things (owner's trade-off for speed).
145	- **Risks & how we watch them:** admins can edit the gate (ability ⚠️ R3.2.2, R3.6 #1; logging 📖 R3.2.2), logged, not prevented;
146	  alerts on ruleset changes and a monthly report of cross-domain approvals on PRs without the
147	  `incident` label. An agent could approve through its engineer's login; no detection found (⚠️). The
148	  required-check app's hosting, key and triggers are open (⚠️ G19).
149	- **Next steps:** rulesets, CODEOWNERS and its validation check in phase 1; the composition of the L3
150	  owner team is open (G17).
151	
152	## 5. References
153	
154	- Framework layer 3 ("Gate = merge to `main`", "Who approves at night"), layer 7 (audit alerts).
155	- Related: ADR-0001, ADR-0004.
156	=================== 0004-risk-stop-on-risky-prod-diffs.md
157	# ADR-0004: Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until a stack owner approves the prod preview
158	
159	- **Status:** Accepted
160	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
161	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (OD8, OD11, OD13)
162	- **Scope:** deploy workflows for Pulumi and Serverless stacks; k0s and Firebase not covered yet
163	
164	## 1. Context
165	
166	With the gate at merge time (ADR-0003), the approver reviews the code change, not the prod diff. A
167	PR may not preview prod, because that would run PR code with state-write and secret access
168	(📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). So a stateful delete or an IAM change can reach prod without anyone
169	seeing its real effect. Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files such as
170	`serverless.yml`, not in separate L3 paths.
171	
172	## 2. Options considered
173	
174	| Option | Pros | Cons |
175	|---|---|---|
176	| A. Accept the gap | No extra step | Destructive diffs applied unseen |
177	| B. Risk stop, approved by the L3 owner team | Specialist review | Often a third person; L3 team must be on call 24/7 |
178	| C. Risk stop, approved by an owner of the stack | Stays at two people; works at night | Less specialist review; compensated by automated checks |
179	
180	## 3. Decision
181	
182	Option C [design]. The deploy job on `main` previews prod. On stateful replace/delete, an IAM
183	change, a network or security-group change, or (from phase 2) an advisory policy finding, it stops
184	and posts the filtered preview. The original author opens a PR (the workflow cannot, because "Allow GitHub Actions to create and
185	approve pull requests" stays off, 📖 R3.3.3) adding
186	`deploy-approvals/<stack>/<sha>.yaml` with the SHA and preview hash; the first approver approves it
187	(OD13). If that approver is unavailable, another stack owner approves; this makes three people and
188	is recorded as a deviation (OD11). After the merge the workflow previews again on the new HEAD and
189	continues only if the hash matches. Serverless uses `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI because
190	differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2). A `mandatory` Pulumi policy violation always
191	blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2).
192	
193	## 4. Consequences
194	
195	- **Positive:** the person who approves now sees the prod diff for the changes that can do lasting
196	  damage. Still two people in the normal case.
197	- **Negative / trade-offs:** while a stack is stopped, later deploys to it stop too (the hash
198	  differs), including an incident fix, until the approval lands or the change is reverted. One more review round when the stop fires.
199	- **Risks & how we watch them:** preview output may not be stable enough to hash (⚠️ Options §8); if
200	  not, compare a structured summary. Until phase 2, the risk stop is the only compensation for OD8;
201	  Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and policy packs follow. k0s and Firebase have no
202	  preview step in this design (⚠️ G1, G2).
203	- **Next steps:** risk stop in the deploy job in phase 1.
204	
205	## 5. References
206	
207	- Framework layer 3 ("Risk stop"), layer 5 (required checks); `work/03-options.md` §1.
208	- Related: ADR-0001, ADR-0003.
209	=================== 0005-break-glass-is-time-limited-jit.md
210	# ADR-0005: Break-glass is a time-limited, approved JIT grant, for incidents only
211	
212	- **Status:** Accepted
213	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
214	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-8; Options §9 Q2; D2; OD7, OD13)
215	- **Scope:** AWS production accounts through IAM Identity Center; k0s and Firebase not covered (G1, G2)
216	
217	## 1. Context
218	
219	Some incidents cannot use the PR path: GitHub or Actions is down, the pipeline is broken, or the
220	operation is not in IaC and has no runbook. Without a defined fallback, people keep standing access
221	"just in case", which ADR-0002 removes.
222	
223	## 2. Options considered
224	
225	| Option | Pros | Cons |
226	|---|---|---|
227	| A. No fallback | Single path | Outage of GitHub blocks every fix; pressure to keep standing access |
228	| B. Standing break-glass account, used first and approved later | Always available | Standing prod write; unapproved use, rejected by the owner (GĐ-8, Options §0.4) |
229	| C. Approved JIT grant, 1-hour role session, command list, reconciled after | Approval before use; time-boxed; traceable | Approves a command list, not an applied change (partial) |
230	
231	## 3. Decision
232	
233	Option C, used only during an incident when the PR path cannot be used.
234	
235	- **Request:** command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub.
236	- **Approval:** the on-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant; the on-call approver counts as
237	  owner of the service (OD13).
238	- **Grant:** `InfraOperator-<service>` [design name], assigned via `CreateAccountAssignment` and removed
239	  via `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2); role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4).
240	- **Execution:** the incident responder types the commands in a terminal without an agent (D2, OD7).
241	- **Example request** (illustrative command ⚠️): "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage.
242	  Run `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
243	  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
244	- **After:** CloudTrail writes in the window are compared with the list; a codify PR follows by a
245	  fixed deadline; drift detection runs until it merges.
246	
247	## 4. Consequences
248	
249	- **Positive:** no standing prod write even for emergencies; every use has an approval, a window and
250	  a reconciliation.
251	- **Negative / trade-offs:** meets the approval rule only partly (owner accepted). "No agent in the
252	  JIT terminal" is a process rule: the grant is reachable from the same laptop.
253	- **Risks & how we watch them:** deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions, so a grant
254	  can run up to about 2 h (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which keeps
255	  the user blocked ≥ 12 h (📖 R2.4.4); no night-time path to apply it is designed yet (⚠️ G20).
256	  Metrics: JIT used where a PR was possible, writes outside the list, late codify PRs (review at 1).
257	- **Next steps:** minimal JIT with per-grant CloudTrail comparison in phase 1; revocation SCP and
258	  automated reconciliation in phase 2.
259	
260	## 5. References
261	
262	- Framework layer 7 ("Break-glass = JIT fallback"); `work/03-options.md` §4b, §9.
263	- Related: ADR-0001, ADR-0002.
264	=================== 0006-mcp-and-plugins-only-from-allowlist.md
265	# ADR-0006: MCP servers and plugins are allowed only from a reviewed, pinned catalogue
266	
267	- **Status:** Accepted
268	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
269	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (framework approval 2026-11-09; rollout priority framing Q8)
270	- **Scope:** Claude Code on all engineer laptops and in CI; Papaya's internal plugin marketplace
271	
272	## 1. Context
273	
274	Local MCP servers, plugins and hooks run with the engineer's access (📖 R1.6.2, R5.5.5); remote MCP
275	servers receive tokens and data. Papaya runs an internal plugin marketplace (brief, Appendix A), and
276	engineers install MCP servers without review (brief); use of Linear and Slack through MCP is assumed
277	(⚠️ G9). An unreviewed server or a plugin update can read the repo, the SSO cache or claim
278	data and send it out.
279	
280	## 2. Options considered
281	
282	| Option | Pros | Cons |
283	|---|---|---|
284	| A. Free choice, guidance only | No friction | No inventory; any server can exfiltrate |
285	| B. Denylist known-bad servers | Low friction | Misses new and changed servers |
286	| C. Allowlist (catalogue) enforced by managed settings | Inventory and supplier records; blocks unknown servers | Up to 5 working days' wait for a new tool (S6) |
287	
288	## 3. Decision
289	
290	Option C. The catalogue is a file in git, changed by PR under the L3 owner team.
291	
292	- **Plugins:** only Papaya's marketplace via managed `strictKnownMarketplaces`, plus
293	  `blockedMarketplaces` (📖 R1.4.2); sources pinned to `ref`/`sha` (📖 R1.4.1b, link only);
294	  `disableSideloadFlags` (📖 R1.4.2); version floor covering the plugin-pin fix of 2.1.179 (📖 R6.2.7).
295	- **MCP:** `allowedMcpServers` with `allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true` (📖 R1.3.1, R1.3.4); match by
296	  `serverUrl` or `serverCommand` (exact argv), never `serverName`, which "is not a security control"
297	  (📖 R1.3.3); `disableClaudeAiConnectors: true` (📖 R1.3.7).
298	- **Review checklist** [design]: publisher, local or remote, what it reads and where it sends data,
299	  supplier-register entry and BAA/DPA status, no token passthrough (📖 R6.4.2), pinned version.
300	  Example entry: `serverCommand` = `["npx", "<package>@<exact-version>"]` [design; placeholder].
301	- **CI:** server-managed settings do not reach a CI job (📖 R1.7.10); CI uses a managed-settings
302	  file on the runner and a fixed MCP set, because `.mcp.json` loads without a prompt in `-p` runs
303	  (📖 R1.3.5).
304	
305	## 4. Consequences
306	
307	- **Positive:** Compliance gets an asset inventory and supplier records (P4c); unknown servers are
308	  refused before they load.
309	- **Negative / trade-offs:** waiting time for new tools; review effort for 1–2 DevSecOps people.
310	- **Risks & how we watch them:** `disableSideloadFlags` does not cover `.mcp.json` or `claude mcp add`
311	  (📖 R1.4.2), so the MCP allowlist must be locked. No per-group targeting in server-managed settings
312	  (📖 R1.1.6). Tool description changes after approval are not covered (⚠️). Without MDM, laptops can
313	  bypass server-managed settings (📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ G11). Evidence: OTel `plugin_installed` /
314	  `plugin_loaded` (📖 R1.4.6).
315	- **Next steps:** catalogue v1 in phase 1 (may slip to phase 2 only with owner agreement).
316	
317	## 5. References
318	
319	- Framework layer 4; layer 8 rollout.
320	- Related: ADR-0007.
321	=================== 0007-agent-settings-are-hygiene-not-the-boundary.md
322	# ADR-0007: Claude Code managed settings are hygiene, not the security boundary
323	
324	- **Status:** Accepted
325	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
326	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-6, Options §0.4; D1, D3; OD4, OD7b, OD12)
327	- **Scope:** Claude Code on laptops (server-managed settings, Team plan) and in CI
328	
329	## 1. Context
330	
331	The brief names "permission prompts turned off" as a problem. It is tempting to make Claude Code
332	settings the main control. But server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not a security
333	boundary" (📖 R1.1.7), local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8), Bash rules are not a boundary
334	(📖 R1.2.6), and on laptops without MDM another login or provider skips server-managed settings
335	(📖 R1.1.7; ⚠️ G11).
336	
337	## 2. Options considered
338	
339	| Option | Pros | Cons |
340	|---|---|---|
341	| 0. Today (brief): some engineers turn prompts off; no organization policy is described (P3c) | No friction | Prompts turned off unnoticed; no evidence |
342	| A. Settings as the boundary (lock everything, block auto mode) | Simple story | Bypassable on laptops; high friction; people work around it |
343	| B. Settings as hygiene; IAM and the CI gate as the boundary | Boundary holds even if settings are bypassed | Settings give weaker guarantees than they appear to |
344	
345	## 3. Decision
346	
347	Option B. The boundary is IAM (ADR-0002) and the merge gate (ADR-0003). Managed settings set safe,
348	uniform defaults:
349	
350	- `permissions.defaultMode` = `"default"` (Manual), with a read-only allowlist that excludes `aws`, `pulumi`,
351	  `serverless` (D1, OD7b; 📖 R6.9.3); auto mode stays available and is measured.
352	- `disableBypassPermissionsMode: "disable"` (📖 R1.2.2); `requiredMinimumVersion` floor (📖 R1.1.13).
353	- Sandbox with `~/.aws` hidden (📖 R1.6.3, R1.6.4) [design]; `sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` kept `true` (OD12, 📖 R5.5.5b).
354	- OTel exporter without prompt content (📖 R1.1.20, R5.5.4).
355	
356	Outside managed settings: the `--restricted` flag (📖 R6.9.1b) in CI, set in the workflow file under
357	CODEOWNERS, and, as a process rule, in the incident-analysis session; a setting cannot force it
358	(📖 R6.9.1) (D3).
359	
360	Phase 1 ships `defaultMode`, the allowlist, bypass removal, the catalogue keys, the version floor and
361	OTel; the rest of the baseline follows in phase 2 (OD4).
362	
363	## 4. Consequences
364	
365	- **Positive:** a bypassed or misconfigured agent still cannot write prod or read PHI. Compliance gets
366	  one organization policy with evidence instead of personal choices.
367	- **Negative / trade-offs:** more prompts than auto mode; a prompt for every `aws` read. S5
368	  ("nobody can turn off all prompts unnoticed") is likely unreachable without MDM (⚠️).
369	- **Risks & how we watch them:** the auto-mode classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions
370	  (📖 R6.3.5); fallback to `disableAutoMode` (📖 R1.2.2) if the planted-injection test steers it (D1). The live
371	  settings are edited in the admin console, not by PR (📖 R1.1.5); an Owner exports them monthly and
372	  diffs them with git until a better method exists (G18).
373	  Until phase 2 there is no sandbox: `~/.aws` is readable and the network open; in auto mode the
374	  classifier is the only gate. `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` run outside the sandbox even later
375	  (📖 R1.6.4; ⚠️ inference), so SSO-token theft remains possible; bounded by ADR-0002.
376	- **Next steps:** phase-1 subset; planted-injection test in phase 3.
377	
378	## 5. References
379	
380	- Framework layer 2; layer 8 rollout; research 6.6 (D1–D3).
381	- Related: ADR-0002, ADR-0006.
382	=================== 0008-oidc-no-long-lived-ci-keys.md
383	# ADR-0008: CI uses OIDC; no long-lived CI keys, with one time-boxed exception
384	
385	- **Status:** Accepted
386	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
387	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (framing Q8; OD1, OD6; target S2)
388	- **Scope:** GitHub Actions deploy workflows to AWS, GCP, k0s and Firebase
389	
390	## 1. Context
391	
392	CI becomes the only routine production writer (ADR-0001), so it is the main target. Repository
393	secrets can be read by anyone with write access (📖 R3.5.3b), which includes every engineer and their
394	agent. A long-lived key there is standing prod write in disguise.
395	
396	## 2. Options considered
397	
398	| Option | Pros | Cons |
399	|---|---|---|
400	| A. Keep stored keys, rotate them | No migration | Standing prod write for all writers |
401	| B. OIDC everywhere, no exception | S2 = 0 | k0s and Firebase may not support it yet (G1, G2) |
402	| C. OIDC for AWS and GCP; a controlled exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials | Removes most keys now | One exception to manage |
403	
404	## 3. Decision
405	
406	Option C.
407	
408	- **AWS:** GitHub OIDC (📖 R3.4.1); the prod role trusts only the `production` environment of the
409	  monorepo (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4), ideally narrowed by `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
410	- **GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization (📖 R3.4.5b).
411	- **k0s/Firebase exception** (OD1, OD6): CI deploy credentials only, until it is checked whether they
412	  can use OIDC. Conditions [design]: a `production` environment secret, never a repository secret
413	  (📖 R3.1.2, R3.1.3); GitHub-hosted runners, because on self-hosted runners environment secrets act
414	  like repository secrets (📖 R3.1.5); if k0s needs a self-hosted runner, it is dedicated to the
415	  `production` deploy and the residual risk is recorded (⚠️ G15); a single source of truth; owner, expiry, rotation.
416	- `GITHUB_TOKEN` default "restricted" (📖 R3.5.3); actions pinned by lockfile or full SHA (📖 R3.5.5).
417	
418	## 4. Consequences
419	
420	- **Positive:** no stored AWS or GCP keys to leak (S2); every deploy credential is tied to a reviewed
421	  workflow on `main`.
422	- **Negative / trade-offs:** one-time migration; slower action updates. The exception remains until
423	  G1/G2 are solved.
424	- **Risks & how we watch them:** admins can change or delete the environment, and a deleted
425	  environment comes back without protection (⚠️ R3.1.4); alerts and a settings comparison cover it.
426	  The GitHub Apps used for CI agents and the required check have their own keys (⚠️ G19).
427	  Runtime credentials inside the cluster are out of the exception (OD6).
428	- **Next steps:** OIDC and removal of stored keys in phase 1; k0s/Firebase credentials moved to
429	  environment secrets before standing prod write is removed.
430	
431	## 5. References
432	
433	- Framework layer 1 ("CI → AWS", "CI → GCP"), layer 5 ("Credentials").
434	- Related: ADR-0001.
435	=================== 0009-agent-stays-outside-phi.md
436	# ADR-0009: The coding agent stays outside PHI; real-data reads are approved per tenant
437	
438	- **Status:** Accepted
439	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
440	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (research 1.9, 5.8 "not extended"; GĐ-9, GĐ-14)
441	- **Scope:** coding-agent sessions on laptops and in CI; production stores of all insurer tenants
442	
443	## 1. Context
444	
445	Papaya holds medical records, national IDs and bank accounts for several insurer tenants in
446	different countries. Claude Team is not shown as BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Partner-uploaded claim
447	documents are both PHI and a prompt-injection vector (research 1.11.4 L6). Neither OWASP nor NIST
448	knows a full prevention for prompt injection (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
449	
450	## 2. Options considered
451	
452	| Option | Pros | Cons |
453	|---|---|---|
454	| A. Agent reads prod data freely | Fastest debugging | PHI in transcripts; injection can exfiltrate; no BAA |
455	| B. Agent never reads any customer data | Simplest rule | Blocks legitimate debugging of non-PHI data |
456	| C. Agent outside PHI; other personal data case by case under an approved, per-tenant grant | Matches the owner's boundary; debugging still possible | Process controls on some paths |
457	
458	## 3. Decision
459	
460	Option C.
461	
462	- **PHI:** never in an agent session. A human reads in a terminal without an agent and gives the
463	  agent a redacted summary. A store that holds PHI counts as PHI unless the agent reads a view without
464	  it [design].
465	- **Other personal data:** readable within an approved request naming one tenant, purpose, store,
466	  window and agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9); approved by an approver ≠ requester and
467	  co-approved by the tenant's data owner [design]; data-read role, 1 h [design]. The same request
468	  applies when a human reads PHI. At night the
469	  on-call approver approves alone and the data owner reviews the grant the next working day [design].
470	- **Partner documents:** reproduced with synthetic documents or de-identified first [design].
471	- **Non-prod:** synthetic or masked only (GĐ-14); no prod copies (S11).
472	
473	This is a target, not a guarantee: "no agent in the PHI terminal" is a process rule [design] with
474	the same weakness as D2, since the grant is reachable from the same laptop.
475	
476	## 4. Consequences
477	
478	- **Positive:** "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM for AWS stores; one record per
479	  exception (S9). Assumes injection succeeds and limits what it can reach.
480	- **Negative / trade-offs:** debugging with redacted or synthetic data; a request for each real read.
481	- **Risks & how we watch them:** of the 17 paths to PHI (research 1.11.4), tickets, chat, pasted text,
482	  admin pages and CI logs are covered by process only; k0s and GCP stores follow the same principle
483	  with mechanisms still open (G1, G3). Per-tenant scoping through session tags (📖 R2.1.8) is
484	  unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️). During a data-read window a stolen SSO
485	  token could open the grant (⚠️, ADR-0007). Data-plane deny actions are incomplete (⚠️ G13). Planted-injection test in
486	  phase 3.
487	- **Next steps:** non-prod data scan and the minimal real-data read flow in phase 1; data-plane SCP in
488	  phase 2.
489	
490	## 5. References
491	
492	- Framework layer 6; layer 1 (SCPs); research 1.9, 1.11.4, 5.8.
493	- Related: ADR-0002, ADR-0006.
494	=================== 0010-risk-level-decides-who-approves.md
495	# ADR-0010: Risk level decides who approves, not how many; non-prod needs no approval
496	
497	- **Status:** Accepted
498	- **Date:** 2026-11-09
499	- **Decided by:** owner of this submission (GĐ-14; OD2, OD3, OD8, OD9)
500	- **Scope:** every change made by engineers and their agents, from non-prod to production
501	
502	## 1. Context
503	
504	Engineering says "Let Claude Code talk to AWS directly" (brief); the need behind it is speed. Compliance's sentence is
505	about production writes only (framing §3.1). A single rule for all changes either slows non-prod for
506	no gain or leaves high-risk prod changes with too light a review. The owner also wants every prod
507	change to need two people, no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it (OD2).
508	
509	## 2. Options considered
510	
511	| Option | Pros | Cons |
512	|---|---|---|
513	| A. Same approval for everything | Simple | Non-prod loop slowed for no gain; high-risk changes get no extra scrutiny |
514	| B. More approvers as risk grows (e.g. two for L3) | More eyes on dangerous changes | Breaks the two-person rule; slower incidents |
515	| C. Risk level narrows who may approve, plus a risk stop; non-prod free | Fast where damage is small; specialist owners where it is large | One reviewer for high-risk changes can miss things |
516	
517	## 3. Decision
518	
519	Option C [design levels]:
520	
521	| Level | What | Approval |
522	|---|---|---|
523	| L0 | Reads: non-prod anything, prod metadata | none |
524	| L1 | Changes in non-prod (synthetic or masked data only, GĐ-14) | none, author only |
525	| L2 | Routine prod change, e.g. Lambda memory 1024 → 2048 MB | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher |
526	| L3 | IAM/SCP, stateful replace/delete, network, workflow and agent-config files, catalogue, advisory policy finding (full list: framework layer 5) | 1 owner of that path |
527	| L3-JIT | Break-glass in an incident | on-call approver ≠ requester (ADR-0005) |
528	| L3-data | Real customer data read | approver ≠ requester + agreement; data-owner co-approval [design] (ADR-0009) |
529	
530	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent-configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for the
531	whole team (OD3). Process-defining paths and the SCP stack are owned by the L3 owner team; IAM or
532	stateful changes inside a domain file are approved by that stack's owners (OD8, OD13). At every level,
533	the risk stop applies to any deploy whose prod diff is risky (ADR-0004).
534	
535	## 4. Consequences
536	
537	- **Positive:** a free non-prod loop for engineers and agents (S4); the same two-person rule for every
538	  prod change, incidents included. Compliance gets a written rule for who may approve what.
539	- **Negative / trade-offs:** one approver for high-risk changes (owner's trade-off for speed);
540	  `CLAUDE.md` edits wait for the L3 owner team, not the domain team that edits them most.
541	- **Risks & how we watch them:** the free loop holds only if non-prod has no real data; a non-prod
542	  store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule until scanned (S11). A risky diff hidden in an L2 PR is
543	  caught by the risk stop, not by the level.
544	- **Next steps:** non-prod data scan and CODEOWNERS with the L3 path list in phase 1; composition of
545	  the L3 owner team is open (G17).
546	
547	## 5. References
548	
549	- Framework layer 3 (levels table), layer 5 (canonical L3 path list), layer 6 (non-prod).
550	- Related: ADR-0003, ADR-0004, ADR-0005, ADR-0009.

1	# Framework: coding agents for DevSecOps at Papaya
2	
3	> Status: v3 after 17 independent review rounds; approved by the owner 2026-11-09 · Updated: 2026-11-09
4	> Audience: a panel of Engineering and Compliance. Each layer ends with what it costs engineers and
5	> what it gives Compliance.
6	
7	## How to read this
8	
9	Eight layers. Each has a **Principle** (tool-independent), **On Papaya's stack** (Pulumi,
10	Serverless Framework, GitHub Actions, AWS, GCP, k0s, Claude Code) and **Audit evidence** (records an
11	auditor can test without asking anyone). Copy-paste detail belongs in `examples/`.
12	
13	| Marker | Meaning |
14	|---|---|
15	| 📖 R*x.y* | Documented. R*x.y* is a ✅/📖 row in `work/02-research.md` that quotes or links the official page (a few rows cite vendor blogs, bulletins or example files instead, e.g. R2.4.1b, R6.3.5, R5.5.4). |
16	| ⚠️ R*x.y* | Inference, open question or "What this means for Papaya" conclusion in the research (sections 1.8, 2.9, 3.6, 3.7, 4.6, 5.6, 5.7, 6.5), or the ⚠️ part of a mixed row. Reasoned, not documented. |
17	| ⚠️ | Not verified at all, e.g. an illustrative command. |
18	| [design] | My proposal, built from documented parts, untested. Treat as ⚠️. |
19	
20	Nothing here was checked locally (✅): this is a design without access to Papaya's systems.
21	**GĐ-n** = assumption in `work/01-problem-framing.md` §4 (owner-confirmed: GĐ-1, 2, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11,
22	14; the others are marked "unconfirmed" where used); **S-n** = success criteria
23	(§5); **P/A-n** = problems (§1); **D1–D3** = owner decisions in research 6.6; **Options §n** =
24	`work/03-options.md`; **G-n** = gaps; **OD-n** = owner decisions on this draft (both at the end).
25	Earlier owner answers are cited with their source: "research 6.9.4 Q4", "framing Q8", "Options §9 Q2".
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 1. The decision in one page
30	
31	Engineering and Compliance disagree only about **writes to production**; reads of metadata and all
32	of non-prod are outside Compliance's sentence (framing §3.1). Real customer data is layer 6.
33	
34	**Chosen approach "A + D2'"** (Options §9, owner decision 2026-11-09):
35	
36	1. **Default path:** every prod change is a pull request, approved by a named human who is not the
37	   author, applied by CI. Incidents included ("IaC first").
38	2. **Fallback (break-glass):** only when the PR path cannot be used, a human gets an approved grant
39	   with a 1-hour role session (effective window up to about 2 h, ⚠️ R2.9 #3) and runs an approved command list in a terminal without an agent (layer 7) [design].
40	3. **Nothing standing:** no human or agent holds standing prod write; no long-lived credentials.
41	
42	| Engineering gets | Compliance gets |
43	|---|---|
44	| A free loop in non-prod: read, change, deploy without approval (non-prod is synthetic or masked, GĐ-14; stores not yet scanned are excluded, layer 6). | Every prod change approved **before** apply by a named human ≠ author (GĐ-8, GĐ-11), enforced in GitHub and AWS IAM, outside the agent (limits below). |
45	| Read-only prod metadata for the agent. | No standing prod write (S1), no long-lived CI keys (S2, with an owner-approved exception for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials, OD1, OD6; storage conditions [design], layer 5). |
46	| Self-service PRs, one approval, same-day ship (S4). | One evidence chain per change; approval and change records ≥ 6 years (📖 R5.2.9; applied to change records ⚠️ R5.7 #2). |
47	| Incident lane: approval wait ≤ 15 min, 24/7 (S7). Decision-to-apply target ≤ 30 min (Options §9); current estimate 11–46 min ⚠️, measured first in rollout. | Agent-side controls as a second layer, not the control of record. |
48	
49	**Where the design falls short, stated openly:**
50	
51	- **The fallback meets the approval rule only partly** (approves a command list, not an applied
52	  change); accepted by the owner (Options §9 Q2). It is a second, process-controlled path, while the
53	  framing asked for one technically enforced path (framing §3.3, Options §7). It stays narrow only
54	  if most incidents are expressible in IaC (unknown, Options §8); layer 7 measures this.
55	- **On GitHub Team nobody sees the prod diff before apply** (⚠️ R4.6 #1; Team assumed, GĐ-5).
56	  Risky prod diffs stop the deploy until an owner of the stack approves the prod preview [design].
57	- **Admins can edit the gate**; logged, not prevented (logging 📖 R3.2.2; ability to edit ⚠️ R3.2.2,
58	  R3.6 #1). An admin's agent has
59	  the same power, because the agent uses its engineer's GitHub login (⚠️ R6.5 #10).
60	- **Some rules are process, not technology:** see "Process rules" in layer 1. The owner's rule
61	  "the PR approver is always an engineer, never an agent" (OD5) is absolute as policy, but on
62	  laptops it is enforced by policy and training, not by a technical control: an agent could approve
63	  through its engineer's login, and no detection was found.
64	- **Incident approvers vs domain review:** code-owner review means an approver must own the file,
65	  at L2 as at L3. So that one on-call primary can approve any deployable path at 2 a.m., the on-call approver
66	  group co-owns every deployable path (owner decision OD9, layer 3). The cost: GitHub accepts an
67	  approval from any listed owner (📖 R3.2.7), so on normal days that group could approve another
68	  domain's PR. Domain review on normal days becomes a process rule with a monthly check, not a
69	  technical control. Because on-call approvers only
70	  approve (OD7), a night incident needs two people awake: the incident responder and the on-call
71	  approver (the backup only replaces an unavailable primary).
72	- **One approver for high-risk changes.** L3 changes (IAM, stateful deletes, workflow files) get one
73	  approver, like L2, but the path is owned by the L3 owner team (or by the stack's owners for L3
74	  content in domain files, OD8), and risky prod diffs stop for a look at
75	  the prod preview (OD2, OD8, layer 3). A single reviewer can miss things; this is the owner's trade-off
76	  for speed.
77	- **k0s and Firebase are weaker:** no prod preview or risk stop, no CloudTrail for k0s changes
78	  (so S3 reconciliation does not cover them), and no break-glass when Actions is down (G1, G2).
79	- **New dependencies on two GitHub Apps** (required check, CI agent): if the required-check app is
80	  down, every merge to `main` is blocked, incident PRs included; that counts as "pipeline
81	  unavailable" for JIT. Their keys and hosting are open (G19).
82	- **HIPAA applicability is a legal question** (⚠️ R1.11.1.11); the design treats Papaya as a
83	  business associate, as the brief implies.
84	
85	**Cross-cutting rules** (owner's balance principle, research 6.8):
86	
87	1. **The boundary is IAM and the CI gate.** Server-managed settings are "a client-side control, not
88	   a security boundary" (📖 R1.1.7); local admins can edit endpoint files (📖 R1.1.8).
89	2. **Assume prompt injection succeeds:** neither OWASP nor NIST knows a full prevention (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.2).
90	3. **Friction where damage is large, none where it is small**, measured, with a time-boxed escape.
91	4. **Evidence by construction:** the path produces the records.
92	
93	### Roles
94	
95	| Role | Rule |
96	|---|---|
97	| Author (engineer + their agent) | Never approves own change; GitHub blocks PR authors from approving (📖 R3.3.1). |
98	| Approver | Always an engineer, never an agent (owner rule, OD5). Named in CODEOWNERS; ≠ author, ≠ last pusher (📖 R3.2.3); for an app-opened PR, ≠ the person who triggered it (⚠️ R3.3.4, layer 5). |
99	| Incident responder | Engineer who diagnoses and writes the fix or the JIT request. Never the on-call approver of the same shift (OD7). |

While on call they only approve: they write no fix and file no JIT request, so the approver is always distinct from the author (OD7). The primary approves; the backup replaces an unavailable primary (OD2). No platform-team membership is required; all engineers follow one agreed approval procedure (OD2). |

102	| Control owner | DevSecOps (1–2 people, GĐ-1); owns policies and metrics; not the only approver. |

107	## Layer 1 — Identity and access
108	
109	**Principle.** Every action traces to one named human. Nobody holds standing prod write: prod is
110	written by the pipeline role, or in the fallback by an approved, time-boxed grant. Prod reads default
111	to metadata. No long-lived credentials. Prod and non-prod are separate boundaries.
112	
113	**On Papaya's stack**
114	
115	- **The engineer's access is the agent's access.** The agent uses the engineer's AWS SSO cache, and
116	  one portal session reaches every role assigned to that engineer (📖 R2.2.1, R2.2.2; token-reuse
117	  detail ⚠️ R2.2.2). A separate
118	  "agent" permission set does not separate them (⚠️ R2.9 #1). The control is what the **engineer**
119	  holds.
120	- **Process rules** that follow from this:
121	  - the JIT terminal runs no agent, though the grant is reachable from the same laptop (owner
122	    accepted as a process control, D2);
123	  - the incident-analysis session is meant to use only read-only roles (D2; `--restricted` per D3,
124	    research 6.9.4 Q2);
125	  - the real-data terminal runs no agent when the store holds PHI [design], same weakness as D2;
126	  - an agent never approves PRs: an owner rule (OD5), enforced on laptops by policy and training.
127	    GitHub blocks self-approval only. The auto-mode default block list
128	    excerpt read names "approving Claude's own pull request" (📖 R6.3.3); whether approving
129	    someone else's PR is blocked is unverified (⚠️), and the list
130	    applies only in auto mode. No detection was found (⚠️; `actor_is_agent` in the audit log has no
131	    documented meaning, R3.5.6).
132	- **IAM Identity Center permission sets** (📖 R2.1.1) [design names]:
133	  - `ProdReadMetadata`: metrics, redacted log groups, configuration; no data-plane read on claim
134	    stores; 1 h session, the minimum (📖 R2.1.4). Until a service's logs are redacted at source
135	    (layer 6), it gets that service's metrics only. Lambda configuration can hold secrets resolved by
136	    Serverless in plain text (⚠️ R4.4.7), so configuration reads are allowed per service only after
137	    its secrets move to runtime resolution (⚠️ R4.6 #7). Cost: until then the agent reads
138	    timeout/memory from the IaC code;
139	  - `NonProdDeveloper`: broad, non-prod accounts only;
140	  - `InfraOperator-<service>`: assigned only by the JIT flow (layer 7), via a partner product, the
141	    TEAM sample (📖 R2.4.1, R2.4.1b) or a small home-built flow (⚠️ R2.4.2) on the documented APIs
142	    `CreateAccountAssignment` / `DeleteAccountAssignment` (📖 R2.4.2);
143	  - no standing prod-write permission set.
144	- **SCPs on the prod OU** [design] (SCPs cap member-account principals, 📖 R2.3.1, R2.3.2):
145	  - deny data-plane reads on claim stores except application roles and the approved data-read role,
146	    by `aws:PrincipalArn` (📖 R2.3.8; pattern ⚠️ R2.9 #4). Actions, e.g. `s3:GetObject`,
147	    `sqs:ReceiveMessage`, `states:GetExecutionHistory`, are incomplete and unchecked (⚠️ G13);
148	  - deny `lambda:UpdateFunctionCode` / `lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration` (⚠️ R4.6 #3) except
149	    CloudFormation `deploymentRole`s, the Pulumi prod deploy role (if Pulumi manages Lambdas) and the
150	    JIT roles. This closes `serverless deploy function`, which changes config outside CloudFormation
151	    (📖 R4.4.4), and needs `deploymentRole` set on every Serverless stack (key 📖 R4.4.5; need ⚠️ R4.6 #3);
152	  - a pre-deployed revocation Deny on `identitystore:UserId` (📖 R2.4.4); protect the org trail (📖 R2.6.2).
153	  - Limits: 10 SCPs per target, 10,240 characters; no SCP applies to the management account
154	    (📖 R2.3.2, R2.3.4), so whatever deploys SCPs there is the most sensitive role (L3 path, held by the L3 owner team only, not co-owned by the on-call group; OD13).
155	- **Sessions/MFA:** portal session length set on purpose; an IdP session can extend it silently
156	  (📖 R2.1.5, R2.1.6). MFA lives in the external IdP if one is used (📖 R2.1.7).
157	- **CI → AWS:** GitHub OIDC, no stored keys (📖 R3.4.1). The prod role trusts only the `production`
158	  environment of the monorepo, in its `sub` format (📖 R3.4.3, R3.4.4; immutable format assumed,
159	  ⚠️ R3.7 A2), ideally customised with the deploy workflow's `job_workflow_ref` (📖 R3.4.5; on Team ⚠️ G10).
160	- **CI → GCP:** Workload Identity Federation restricted to Papaya's GitHub organization, which Google
161	  requires (📖 R3.4.5b).
162	- **k0s, GCP and Firebase for humans:** same principles; mechanisms not researched (G1–G3). Today
163	  k0s is reached with kubeconfigs, no SSO (GĐ-4, unconfirmed). Interim: no admin kubeconfig and no GCP
164	  owner role on laptops; prod deploys only from CI. Firebase is not on the GCP BAA list (📖 R5.5.3), so
165	  Firebase Hosting must hold no PHI (⚠️ R5.7 #7).
166	
167	**Audit evidence.** Identity Center assignment export (S1); CloudTrail `CreateAccountAssignment` /
168	`DeleteAccountAssignment` per grant (📖 R2.4.2), linked to its approval by request ID [design]; SCPs
169	and trust policies as Pulumi code; IAM Access Analyzer `check-no-new-access` on policy PRs
170	(📖 R2.8.1; from phase 2); quarterly access review of permission sets and GitHub admins.
171	
172	**Cost / value.** Engineers lose standing prod write and keep a free non-prod loop. Prod reads stay
173	fast for metrics and metadata, but shrink during the transition: because the engineer's access is the
174	agent's access, from phase 1 the engineer too loses raw logs and configuration of services not yet
175	redacted or moved to runtime secrets. Configuration values come from the IaC code instead (layer 1
176	above); raw logs that may hold customer data need an L3-data grant. The data owner is not on the
177	on-call schedule, so at night the grant is approved by the on-call approver alone and the data owner
178	reviews it the next working day [design]; the wait still counts against S7. This is
179	the largest cost of the first months. Compliance gets least privilege that is enforced.

183	## Layer 2 — Agent runtime controls
184	
185	**Principle.** Agent-side controls are hygiene, not the boundary. They are central, versioned in git
186	and the same for everyone. Defaults are safe; overrides are measured. The session that reads
187	untrusted content holds as little power as possible (📖 R6.1.2).
188	
189	**On Papaya's stack**
190	
191	- **Delivery:** server-managed settings (available on Team, 📖 R1.1.5) for all laptops. With MDM, also
192	  an endpoint file; by default one managed source supplies most keys, so the two must carry the same
193	  keys or use `managedSourcesBehavior: "merge"` (📖 R1.1.3, R1.1.4). MDM is unknown; both are prepared.
194	- **Baseline** (template: Anthropic's `settings-hipaa.json`, 📖 R5.5.4). All keys 📖 at the row cited. Only the phase-1 subset in layer 8 ships first; the other keys (sandbox, `allowManagedHooksOnly`, credential denies, `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly`, `allowedProviders`, `forceLoginOrgUUID`, the `ask` rule for WebFetch, and the other deny rules) arrive in phase 2 (OD4):

199	  | `permissions.allow` | Read-only commands Papaya uses, to cut prompts (R6.9.3). The HIPAA template denies WebFetch (R5.5.4); "ask" is a deliberate deviation so that documentation lookups still work. |

It does not end running sessions and fails open on a bad value (R1.1.13). |

The HIPAA README says to set `false` if policy needs a person to approve each command (R5.5.5b); cost of `false`: a prompt per command. |

211	- **Trade-off on AWS credentials [design].** With `~/.aws` hidden from the sandbox, the plan is to
212	  list `aws`, `pulumi` and `serverless` in `sandbox.excludedCommands`. Excluded commands run "with
213	  full access" (📖 R1.6.4), which likely includes the network (⚠️ inference). How the list matches
214	  commands (prefix or text, and chained commands) is not researched (⚠️). This is worse than an
215	  egress channel: `pulumi preview` runs the Pulumi program and `serverless` loads its config and
216	  plugins, all code in the repo that the agent can edit, so excluding them lets repo code run
217	  outside the sandbox with network access and with `~/.aws` readable (⚠️ inference). For these
218	  commands the sandbox gives no protection. And an injected `aws` command could send out the SSO
219	  token cache itself. That token likely opens every role assigned to the engineer for the rest of the
220	  portal session (📖 R2.1.5; token reuse ⚠️ R2.2.2), probably including JIT or data-read grants added
221	  later in that session (⚠️ inference). Mitigations [design]: a short portal session (📖 R2.1.5); end
222	  the existing portal session and sign in fresh **before** a JIT or data-read grant is created
223	  (whether ending a session invalidates a token already stolen is unverified ⚠️; ending it does not
224	  end role sessions, 📖 R2.4.3); an SCP that denies writes to resources outside Papaya's organization using
225	  `aws:ResourceOrgID` (key 📖 R2.3.8), on every OU, since the token can be stolen from a non-prod
226	  session; legitimate writes to outside resources need exceptions (⚠️ not inventoried). That SCP only stops Papaya's own credentials writing to a
227	  foreign bucket; it does not stop a command that sends the token to a non-AWS endpoint or uses the
228	  attacker's credentials (⚠️ inference). Prefer running `pulumi` and `serverless` against real
229	  accounts only in CI; on laptops keep them to non-prod roles, and move them into the phase-3
230	  container. Residual risk: token theft during a session. It is accepted
231	  because the engineer holds no **standing** prod write and no **standing** PHI read; during a JIT
232	  or data-read window the protection is the process rule in layer 1 (D2). Stronger option, phase 3:
233	  a separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions
234	  (⚠️ R6.5 #2).

274	## Layer 3 — Change workflow by risk level
275	
276	**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
277	reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
278	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. Every prod change needs two people, and
279	no more by default: one who makes it and one who approves it; the on-call backup only replaces an
280	unavailable primary (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of that path), not how
281	many. Separately, any prod diff that looks risky stops the deploy, whatever its level; that adds a
282	second approval by an owner of the same stack, which keeps it to two people (OD8). Confirmed by the owner
283	(OD13): the original author opens the approval PR and the first approver
284	approves it. If the first approver is unavailable, another owner of the stack approves; that makes
285	three people and is recorded as a deviation, counted monthly (OD11). A cross-team PR needs one
286	approval, as GitHub accepts one on-call group member for files of several owner teams (OD10,
287	OD9, 📖 R3.2.7); domain review there is a recommendation, counted in the monthly report. A real-data read is not a change and has its own rule, L3-data. Incidents use the same
288	path with faster people, not fewer security checks.
289	
290	| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
291	|---|---|---|---|---|
292	| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
293	| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
294	| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
295	| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue and the rest of the canonical list in layer 5; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher. L3 paths (workflow and agent-config files, catalogue, the SCP stack): the L3 owner team only (OD13); IAM-only stacks are deployable, so the L3 owner team plus the on-call group (OD9). L3 content inside a domain file (an IAM statement in `serverless.yml`, a stateful delete): the stack's owner, then the risk stop (OD8). In incidents: the on-call approver for deployable paths (OD9); paths that define the process (CODEOWNERS, agent config, catalogue, workflows) wait for the L3 owner team | same path; for IaC changes the risk stop also applies; workflow and agent-config files have no prod diff |
296	| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b); incidents only, as the owner accepted it (Options §9 Q2); the on-call approver counts as owner of the service in the request (OD13) | layer 7 |
297	| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | an approver ≠ requester and an agreement (GĐ-9); data-owner co-approval [design], beyond GĐ-9; at night, see layer 6 | layer 6 |
298	
299	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
300	the whole team (OD3). With code-owner review on, every PR, L2 included, needs an approval from an
301	owner of the files it touches (📖 R3.2.3, R3.2.7; per-file behaviour ⚠️ not a separate research row).
302	What differs at L3 is **which team** owns the path: L3 paths are owned in CODEOWNERS by a designated
303	L3 owner team (deployable L3 paths also by the on-call group, OD9), L2 paths by their domain team; and IaC changes at L3 meet the
304	risk stop. Most IAM, network and stateful changes sit inside domain files, so they are approved by
305	the stack's owners, not the L3 team (OD8); automated checks make up for this: IAM Access Analyzer
306	`check-no-new-access` (📖 R2.8.1) and the Pulumi policy pack (📖 R4.2.2), both from phase 2 (layer 5). Cost: changes to `CLAUDE.md` (where D3 puts shared knowledge) need the L3 owner team, not
307	the domain team that edits it most.
308	
309	**On Papaya's stack**
310	
311	- **Gate = merge to `main`.** On Team, environment reviewers do not exist for private repos
312	  (📖 R3.1.2). Ruleset on `main`: PR required, 1 approval, code-owner review, dismiss stale approvals,
313	  approval by someone other than the last pusher, required checks from a pinned source app, no force
314	  push, empty bypass list (📖 R3.2.2, R3.2.3, R3.2.5). Branch up to date before merge, since there is
315	  no merge queue (⚠️ R4.6 #1; whether updating drops approvals is open, Options §8).
316	- **L3 approvals [design]:** CODEOWNERS plus code-owner review only, no path-based required
317	  reviewers rule. That rule (📖 R3.2.4) asks for approvals from specific teams, which the on-call
318	  group would not satisfy at night, and how it combines several teams is not researched (⚠️), so it
319	  would break OD9 or add a third person. GitHub stops the author from approving (📖 R3.3.1). A required check with a pinned source app (📖 R3.2.5), set by a dedicated GitHub App that reacts to review events and is the pinned source [design; hosting, key storage and whether its key counts against S2 are not researched, ⚠️ G19], adds what
320	  the rules cannot: for app-opened PRs it excludes the person who triggered the agent, and it counts
321	  only human approvals, since an app's approval might count (⚠️ R3.3.4, R3.7 A3). A workflow
322	  instead of an app is weaker: pinning the source to GitHub Actions likely lets any workflow set a
323	  check of the same name, and the trigger that runs on review events from trusted code is not
324	  researched (⚠️ G19).
325	- **Who approves at night (OD9):** a fixed GitHub team with write permission (owners without it
326	  are silently not assigned, 📖 R3.2.7; the CODEOWNERS validation check covers this), the on-call approvers, is listed as
327	  co-owner on every deployable path in CODEOWNERS (infrastructure and service code), next to the
328	  domain team. Confirmed by the owner (OD13): the group does **not** co-own the paths that
329	  define the process (`.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md` and agent config, catalogue); those stay
330	  with the L3 owner team only. If a broken workflow blocks a night fix, the pipeline counts as
331	  unavailable and the JIT fallback applies (layer 7). One primary and one backup from that team are on call. Technically any member can approve any
332	  path; by rule the primary approves and the backup only if the primary is unavailable (OD2).
333	  Membership is fixed, not changed per shift [design]. GitHub team membership is set in organization
334	  settings, not by a PR; managing it as code (e.g. with Pulumi's GitHub provider) and the audit
335	  event for a membership change are not researched (⚠️ G16). Meanwhile the layer-7 settings
336	  comparison includes the group's member list. Cost: an approval from any
337	  listed owner satisfies code-owner review (📖 R3.2.7), so on normal days a member could approve
338	  another domain's PR, on or off shift. Mitigation [design]: process rule "approve another
339	  domain's PR only if it carries the `incident` label and you are on shift", and a monthly report of
340	  every cross-domain approval by group members on PRs without that label (layer 7). Whether Papaya's team size allows full coverage is unknown
341	  (§1, S7).
342	- **Risk stop [design]:** applies to every deploy, whatever the level. The deploy job previews prod;
343	  on stateful replace/delete, an IAM change, a network or security-group change, or an advisory
344	  policy finding (from phase 2) it stops and posts the filtered preview. The original author opens a second PR that adds
345	  `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<sha>.yaml` (`<sha>` = the stopped commit) holding that SHA and the
346	  preview hash; the workflow does not open it, because the setting that lets Actions create and approve PRs stays
347	  off (📖 R3.3.3; ⚠️ R3.6 #3). CODEOWNERS on `deploy-approvals/<stack>/` names the owners of that stack and the
348	  on-call group (OD8, OD9). The approver is ≠ author and may be the first PR's approver, who now sees
349	  the prod diff. Merging it triggers the deploy on the new HEAD, which previews again and continues
350	  only if the hash matches the approved one; if another PR merged in between, the hash differs and
351	  the deploy stops again (Options §1; hash stability ⚠️ Options §8). Cost: while a stack is
352	  stopped, later merges to that stack stop too until a matching approval lands; in an incident, a
353	  risky change already waiting on `main` blocks the fix for the same stack until it is approved or
354	  reverted. A
355	  `mandatory` policy violation always blocks `pulumi up` (📖 R4.2.2): the fix is a code change, or a
356	  change to the policy pack through its own L3 PR. Preview output is filtered for
357	  outputs and secrets before it is posted (Options §1; ⚠️ R4.6 #2).
358	- **Merge approval = deploy approval** only if (⚠️ R3.6 #1, from 📖 R3.1.3, R3.4.5c): `production`
359	  allows only `main`; only the reusable deploy workflow (under CODEOWNERS) references it; no ref/SHA
360	  inputs; no `issue_comment`, `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` triggers; one concurrency group
361	  per stack without `cancel-in-progress` (📖 R4.1.4).
362	- **Pulumi:** PRs preview non-prod only, because a prod preview runs PR code with state-write and
363	  secret access (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #2). On `main`: prod preview, then `pulumi up` with the
364	  policy pack, which stops on a mandatory violation (📖 R4.2.2). Prod runs allow no `--skip-preview`
365	  (📖 R4.1.2) and no targeting, replace, `state`, `import`, `destroy` (⚠️ R4.6 #3, G12). Pulumi Cloud,
366	  if used: OIDC via `pulumi/auth-actions`, no stored token (📖 R4.1.4).
367	- **Serverless v4:** `serverless package`; `serverless diff --json` (sf-core ≥ 4.37.0), parsed by CI
368	  because differences do not change the exit code (📖 R4.4.2); `serverless deploy --package`
369	  (📖 R4.4.3); a least-privilege `deploymentRole`, which cannot be removed later and is usable by
370	  anyone who may operate the stack (📖 R4.4.5), so JIT roles get no stack-operation rights.
371	- **State:** writable by deploy roles (and possibly the drift role, layer 7); Pulumi
372	  secrets via `awskms` on a DIY backend (📖 R4.3.3, R4.3.4; ⚠️ R4.6 #7).
373	- **k0s [design]:** manifests in the monorepo, applied by CI; no write RBAC for humans or agents in
374	  prod; read roles exclude logs and exec in namespaces with claim data (mechanism: G1). The risk
375	  stop is described for Pulumi and Serverless only; for k0s manifests (RBAC changes are the IAM
376	  equivalent) a `kubectl diff`-based stop is a candidate, not researched (⚠️ G1). Firebase deploys
377	  have no preview step in this design (⚠️ G2).
378	- **Incident lane:** label `incident`, on-call approver paged, security checks always run (S10), only
379	  slow unrelated tests skipped [design]. A required check skipped by a path filter may stay
380	  pending and block the merge (open, Options §8); this directly affects S7.
381	
382	**Example: Lambda timeouts at 2 a.m.** (Options §6)
383	
384	The incident responder is engineer E; the on-call approver is R (a backup replaces R only if R is
385	unavailable).
386	
387	1. E's incident-analysis session reads metrics and redacted logs and proposes `timeout` 30 → 90 s,
388	   memory 1024 → 2048 MB, and a larger visibility timeout on the source queue (ratio ⚠️ Options §8).
389	2. A second session (edit tools; not meant to use prod roles) edits `serverless.yml`, runs
390	   `serverless diff` on non-prod, and opens a PR labelled `incident` as E.
391	3. R, a co-owner of `serverless.yml` through the on-call group (OD9), reviews the diff. If R
392	   catches a missing queue change, R does not fix it (OD7): E pushes the fix, the stale approval is
393	   dismissed, and R approves again, one more review round (Options §6). E merges.
394	4. The deploy workflow packages, previews prod, finds no risky change, deploys with the OIDC role.
395	5. Estimate 11–46 min (⚠️ Options §6) against ≤ 30 min: measured first in rollout.
396	
397	**Audit evidence.** The PR (diff, approvers, checks); run log and preview artifact, exported because
398	retention is unverified (⚠️ G7); deploy-role CloudTrail events; all linked by commit SHA and run ID.
399	
400	**Cost / value.** One approver for every prod change, from the owners of the path; two approvals,
401	usually by the same approver, when the risk stop fires (OD13; OD11). Cross-team PRs: one approval (OD10). None in non-prod.
402	Compliance gets four-eyes enforced by GitHub. Gap: on Team the prod diff is not seen before apply.

447	checks as human code (S10).

453	  "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests" off (📖 R3.3.3). Serverless License Key in
454	  SSM, read by the deploy role (sf ≥ 4.4.19, 📖 R4.4.8). Until G1/G2 are solved, k0s and Firebase

525	## Layer 6 — Data protection and prompt-injection defence
526	
527	**Principle.** The design keeps PHI from reaching the coding agent (owner decision, research 1.9).
528	Some paths rely on process (below), so this is a target, not a guarantee. Other customer
529	personal data is outside that hard boundary ("not extended", research 5.8): the agent reads metadata
530	by default and may read such data case by case under GĐ-9. Real-data reads are approved, name one
531	tenant, are time-boxed, and need an agreement (BAA/DPA, partner contract) (GĐ-9). Everything read
532	from outside is untrusted. Non-prod is synthetic or masked (GĐ-14).
533	
534	**On Papaya's stack**
535	
536	- **Paths to PHI** (research 1.11.4 lists 17):
537	  - AWS stores: closed by identity, through `ProdReadMetadata` as the only standing prod role from
538	    phase 1 (existing broad read roles are removed) and the SCP from phase 2
539	    (layer 1); no Aurora credentials, no prod exec, no `lambda:InvokeFunction` for agent-usable roles
540	    [design; actions ⚠️ G13];
541	  - k0s logs/exec and GCP stores (L1, L11, L13): same principle, mechanism open (G1, G3);
542	  - tickets/chat via MCP, pasted text, internal admin pages, prod AI traces, fixtures, CI logs (L5,
543	    L8–L10, L12, L14): process and hygiene only;
544	  - logs redacted at source with raw payloads in a separate log group; alerts carry IDs, not payloads [design].
545	- **Real-data request** [design]: tenant, purpose, store, window, agreement; approved by the data owner
546	  and an approver ≠ requester; JIT data-read role, 1 h. At night the data owner is not on call: the
547	  on-call approver approves alone and the data owner reviews the grant the next working day. This
548	  applies to non-PHI and PHI alike; for PHI the reader is still a human without an agent. Per-tenant scoping through session tags
549	  (📖 R2.1.8) is unresolved, because tags come from user attributes (⚠️).
550	  - **PHI:** a human reads in a terminal without an agent (process rule, layer 1); the agent gets a
551	    redacted summary. This
552	    narrows GĐ-9 because the agent stays outside PHI scope (research 1.9) and Team is not shown as
553	    BAA-covered (⚠️ R1.11.3.4). Enterprise + BAA only for a separate environment if needed (research 1.9).
554	  - **Non-PHI personal data:** the agent may read it within the approved request (GĐ-9). Claim
555	    tables mix health, ID and bank data (research 1.11.4 L2), so a store that holds PHI is treated as
556	    PHI unless the agent reads a view or extract without PHI [design].
557	- **Partner-uploaded claim documents (A7b):** never in an agent session raw; reproduce with synthetic
558	  documents, or de-identify first [design]. The document is PHI and an injection vector (research
559	  1.11.4 L6).
560	- **Injection** (these lower frequency; layers 1 and 3 limit impact): Manual by default (sandboxed Bash runs without a prompt, layer 2); the auto-mode
561	  classifier missed 17 % of 52 real overeager actions and 5.7 % of 1,000 synthetic exfiltration
562	  attempts (📖 R6.3.5). Broad allowed domains such as `github.com` are a documented exfiltration path
563	  (📖 R6.3.7). The incident session has no WebFetch, likely no edit tools (layer 2), and runs outside
564	  the repo, but its Bash can still write locally and send data out through excluded
565	  commands (layer 2), including the SSO token cache; "no standing write, no PHI read" limits what
566	  the token opens, except during a JIT or data-read window (layer 2 mitigations). Shared knowledge
567	  goes in `CLAUDE.md` under review; auto memory is exempt from the protected-path rules unless `--restricted` (📖 R6.3.11, D3).
568	- **Tenants:** one tenant per data-read grant; a session that read one tenant's data does not post to
569	  shared places without review (⚠️ R6.5 #8, process). Logical separation in shared accounts is assumed
570	  (GĐ-3, unconfirmed).
571	- **Non-prod:** no prod copies (S11). A scan of non-prod stores runs at the start of phase 1 (tool:
572	  G4); a store not yet scanned follows the L3-data rule (GĐ-14: until cleaned, non-prod follows the GĐ-9 data-read rule). Cost: until scanned, that store is
573	  not part of the free loop.
574	- **Local stores:** transcripts and memory hold what the agent read (research 1.11.4); set
575	  `cleanupPeriodDays` (30 in the HIPAA sample, 📖 R5.5.4; what it deletes ⚠️).
576	- **Cross-border (Vietnam example):** processing data collected in Vietnam on a platform abroad is a
577	  transfer (📖 R5.4.5); agent flows, including employee names in logs and transcripts, update the
578	  transfer impact assessment (⚠️ R5.7 #4, needs Papaya legal).
579	
580	**Audit evidence.** SCP/IAM text as the written access rule for sensitive data (📖 R5.4.3; ⚠️ R5.7 #5);
581	data-read requests and the data-read role's CloudTrail; planted-injection reports (layer 8); non-prod
582	scan results (S11).
583	
584	**Cost / value.** Debugging with redacted and synthetic data; a request for the rare real-data read.
585	Compliance gets "minimum necessary" (📖 R1.11.1.8) enforced by IAM for AWS stores (fully from phase 2;
586	actions ⚠️ G13) and by process
587	elsewhere, and a record per exception (S9).

592	
593	**Principle.** One tamper-evident evidence chain per prod change. One routed alert channel with a
594	named on-call, approvers included. Unapproved change is detected (drift, reconciliation). Break-glass
595	is approved before use, time-boxed and reconciled after.
596	
597	**On Papaya's stack**
598	
599	- **Audit stores:**
600	  - organization CloudTrail to a log-archive account with integrity validation (📖 R2.6.2, R2.6.4,
601	    R2.6.5); change records ≥ 6 years; raw-log retention for Papaya's compliance owner (⚠️ R5.7 #2).
602	    Data events only on PHI buckets, prod Lambda invoke and prod SQS (cost 📖 R2.6.3; selection
603	    ⚠️ R2.9 #5), which makes the archive
604	    PHI-bearing (⚠️ research 1.11.4 L15). CloudTrail Lake is closed to new customers (📖 R2.6.6);
605	  - GitHub org audit log kept 180 days, so exported (📖 R3.5.6);
606	  - alerts on `repository_ruleset.update`, `environment.update_protection_rule`,
607	    `environment.remove_protection_rule`, `environment.delete`, `protected_branch.policy_override`
608	    (📖 R3.5.6, R3.1.4; selection ⚠️ R3.6 #1). UI changes to the branch policy may leave no event, and a
609	    deleted `production` environment comes back unprotected (⚠️ R3.1.4): a job compares live settings
610	    with an expected copy (G8);
611	  - Aurora SQL is likely invisible to CloudTrail (⚠️ R2.7.1): Database Activity Streams, alerts on
612	    lost-record events (📖 R2.7.2; Serverless v2 ⚠️), stream treated as PHI (⚠️ R2.7.3);
613	  - Claude Code OTel without prompt content (layer 2).
614	- **Change record [design]:** keyed by commit SHA or JIT request ID; links PR, approvals, run ID,
615	  preview and CloudTrail events. Monthly reconciliation: every prod write event matches a record
616	  approved before apply (S3). Actor: `onBehalfOf.userId` where present, else session name plus
617	  directory lookup (📖 R2.5.1; ⚠️ R2.5.3).
618	- **Drift [design]:** its own role, trusted only from a `drift` environment on `main`; it can read
619	  prod secrets in state, which is noted (⚠️ R4.6 #2). Scheduled `pulumi preview --refresh
620	  --expect-no-changes` or `pulumi refresh --preview-only` (📖 R4.1.1, R4.3.1, R4.3.2). On a DIY S3
621	  backend, preview needs state-write permission (📖 R4.3.3); whether a refresh preview writes more
622	  than locks is open (⚠️ R4.6 #2, G14). So either the drift role gets state write (and the same
623	  trust care as the deploy role), or Pulumi Cloud drift detection is used (📖 R4.3.2, Pro+). The
624	  latter runs on Pulumi Deployments, which holds credentials to prod, so it re-opens a side path that
625	  layer 5 excludes and needs the same trust narrowing and audit (📖 R4.4.9; ⚠️ R4.6 #6). CloudFormation
626	  drift detection, explicitly set properties only (📖 R4.4.6). No auto-remediation: it is an unreviewed
627	  `pulumi up --refresh` (📖 R4.3.2). Each finding gets an actor and a ticket.
628	- **On-call:** phase 1 delivers the named approver schedule (primary + backup engineers, 24/7), as
629	  decided in framing round 1, and, because of OD7, a minimal incident-responder schedule; the
630	  latter extends that decision. The primary approves; the backup steps in only if the primary is
631	  unavailable (OD2). On-call approvers only approve during their shift; the fix is written by an
632	  incident responder (OD7). Alert routing and the
633	  rest of on-call follow in phase 2 (tools: G5); in phase 1 the responder calls the approver by phone from the published schedule.
634	- **Break-glass = JIT fallback** [design unless marked]:
635	
636	  | Step | Rule |
637	  |---|---|
638	  | When | Only during an incident (Options §9 Q2), when the PR path cannot be used: operation not in IaC and no runbook; GitHub/Actions down; pipeline broken. The approver refuses JIT for anything expressible in IaC while the pipeline works, and records why. Outside incidents, an operation not in IaC waits for IaC or a runbook. |
639	  | Request | Command list, scope, reason, incident link, in a channel that does not depend on GitHub. |
640	  | Approval | On-call approver ≠ requester, before the grant (Options §4b; OD7; backup rule OD2). |
641	  | Grant | `InfraOperator-<service>`; role session 1 h (📖 R2.1.4). Deleting the assignment likely stops only new sessions (⚠️ R2.4.2, R2.9 #3), so the real window can approach 2 h; ending the portal session does not end role sessions (📖 R2.4.3). An immediate stop needs the revocation SCP, which must keep the user blocked for at least 12 h (📖 R2.4.4). Applying it is a management-account change held by the L3 owner team only, and no night-time path for it is designed yet (⚠️ G20): until one exists, a misused grant may run to the end of its window. Candidate: a pre-approved revocation runbook for one named L3 owner reachable by phone, or an org-wide `aws:TokenIssueTime` Deny as kill switch (⚠️ R2.9 #3). |
642	  | Execution | The grant goes to the requester (the incident responder), who types the commands; no agent in that terminal (D2). D2 said the on-call person runs them; OD7 moves that to the responder, since on-call engineers only approve. |
643	  | After | A job compares CloudTrail writes in the window with the list; a codify PR within a fixed deadline (as soon as GitHub is back); drift detection until it merges. |
644	  | Identity Center outage | Emergency SAML federation to roles, built and tested in advance (📖 R2.1.11; ⚠️ R2.9 #2); no user mapped until an approved activation, which is alerted. |
645	
646	  **Example request (illustrative command ⚠️):** "INC-123, ECS service `claims-api`, Actions outage. Run
647	  `aws ecs update-service --cluster <prod-cluster> --service <svc> --force-new-deployment`. Scope
648	  `InfraOperator-claims`, 1 h."
649	
650	  **Metrics** (Options §7; starting thresholds ⚠️ to calibrate): JIT used where a PR was possible
651	  (review at 1); writes outside the list (review at 1); codify PRs late (review at 1); grants per
652	  month and share of incidents needing non-IaC operations (review above about 25 %, a value new in
653	  this draft). On a breach,
654	  make the PR lane faster or add a runbook; do not widen JIT.
655	- **Roadmap:** runbooks for repeated non-IaC operations, if SSM Automation's approval step meets three
656	  conditions (Options §2; outside 02-research, G6); break-glass from an environment without the agent
657	  (D2, ⚠️).
658	
659	**Audit evidence.** Validated CloudTrail; exported GitHub audit log; change records and monthly
660	reconciliation (S3, S8 ≤ 30 min); JIT requests, reconciliations, codify PRs; drift tickets; on-call
661	schedule and approval waits (S7); monthly report of cross-domain approvals by on-call group members
662	on PRs without the `incident` label (OD9).
663	
664	**Cost / value.** The incident lane is slower than direct access (estimated 11–46 vs 2–20 min,
665	Options §6), and JIT needs a written command list. Compliance gets approval before apply even in
666	incidents, plus detection.

668	---
669	
670	## Layer 8 — Governance and rollout
671	
672	**Principle.** Every control has an owner, a metric and a review date. Policies are files changed by
673	PR. Access is never removed before its replacement works. Controls are tested against realistic
674	attacks.
675	
676	**On Papaya's stack**
677	
678	- **Owners:** DevSecOps (framework, managed settings, catalogue, metrics); a platform team or named
679	  engineers (deploy workflows, rulesets, pipelines; whether Papaya has a platform team is unknown ⚠️); Compliance (evidence review, supplier register, Statement of
680	  Applicability); engineering leads (decide CODEOWNERS content; changes to it are approved by the L3 owner team); engineering management (on-call schedule).
681	- **Policy as code:** catalogue, SCPs, trust policies, CODEOWNERS and workflows are files under
682	  CODEOWNERS. Settings that live outside files are kept as an expected copy in git and compared with
683	  the live state: GitHub settings (⚠️ R3.6 #1; G8) and Claude managed settings, which are edited in
684	  the admin console (📖 R1.1.5; comparison method in layer 2). Few GitHub admins and Claude org
685	  Owners, reviewed quarterly.
686	- **Metrics:** S1–S11 exactly as in framing §5; this framework adds the JIT metrics (layer 7) and the
687	  prompt metrics (layer 2). S2 and S5 have caveats (OD1; layer 2).
688	- **Rollout** (≈ 90 days, GĐ-12 unconfirmed). Framing Q8 (round 1): (1) remove long-lived CI credentials,
689	  (2) narrow standing prod access, (3) MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list before or with (2).
690	
691	  | Phase | Days | Items, in order |
692	  |---|---|---|
693	  | 1 | 0–30 | Measure the incident PR lane on one service (first task once that service has an OIDC deploy workflow, Options §9), including the prompt for each `aws` read, which the allowlist excludes (layer 2). Rulesets, CODEOWNERS and its validation check; the required-check app, before any agent workflow may open PRs (G19); remove human write kubeconfigs for prod k0s (interim, layer 1); phase-1 S10 checks (secret scanning, dependency check, SAST; Access Analyzer and policy packs follow in phase 2, so until then OD8 relies on the risk stop alone). 695	  | 3 | 60–90 | Planted-injection test on the real configuration (📖 R6.1.1, R6.1.5; ⚠️ R6.5 #12); a deliberate trade-off: auto mode runs from day 1 (D1) without this data, and until then only D1's other fallback triggers apply; auto-mode non-prod environment (D1 c); separate OS user or container for prod-reading sessions; first ISO evidence pack; 90-day review of D1–D3. |

698	  people (GĐ-1) plus the owners of deploy workflows, within ~90 days overall (GĐ-12, unconfirmed). This is

767	| OD1 | Exception to S2 = 0 for k0s/Firebase deploy credentials? | Yes, provided each credential has a single source of truth. (The first reason given, continuous scale-in/scale-out, concerns runtime credentials; OD6 narrowed the scope.) |

## 6. Kịch bản: sửa cấu hình Lambda trên prod lúc 2 giờ sáng

**Bối cảnh chung (giả định để so sánh):**
- Function `claims-doc-extract` (tên giả định) xử lý message từ SQS.
- Một partner bắt đầu gửi file lớn hơn, nên function timeout hàng loạt, message quay lại queue, backlog tăng. Alarm kêu.
- Bản sửa: tăng `timeout` 30s → 90s, `memorySize` 1024 → 2048. Cả hai được khai báo rõ trong `serverless.yml`.
  Giả định queue nguồn cũng được khai báo trong cùng `serverless.yml`. Nếu queue nằm ở stack khác (ví dụ Pulumi), A
  phải sửa hai stack và lo thứ tự deploy; lợi thế "một PR, một lần deploy" của A yếu đi.
- Bẫy có thật: visibility timeout của queue nguồn phải đủ lớn so với timeout của function (AWS khuyến nghị ≥ 6 lần;
  ⚠️ nhớ từ docs, chưa mở trang). Agent có thể bỏ sót; đây là chỗ người duyệt có giá trị.
- Người trực: engineer E. Người duyệt trực: R (người khác).
- **Thời gian chẩn đoán không tính** ở mọi phương án, kể cả D (ở D, chẩn đoán chạy trên agent hosted). Thời gian khởi
  động runtime của D được tính, vì đó là chi phí riêng của D.

### A — PR-only

1. E nhận page. E mở **session phân tích**: `--restricted`, `--tools "Bash,Read,Grep,Glob"`, identity read-only
   metadata (D3, 02-research 6.9.4 Q2). Agent chạy `aws lambda get-function-configuration`, đọc metric và log đã che, rồi chẩn đoán.
2. E mở **session thứ hai** có Edit và git/gh, không có identity prod. Session này nhận bản tóm tắt chẩn đoán, không
   đọc lại log thô [TK]. Agent sửa `serverless.yml` (timeout, memory, kèm visibility timeout nếu cùng stack) và chạy
   `serverless diff` trên non-prod.
   - Lệnh này cần sf-core ≥ 4.37.0, và khác biệt không làm exit code khác 0, nên CI phải tự parse `--json` (02-research 4.4.2 ✅).
3. Agent mở PR bằng identity của E, nhãn `incident`. Security checks chạy đủ.
4. R được page, xem diff (GitHub Mobile duyệt được PR là ⚠️ chưa kiểm) và approve.
5. E merge. Workflow deploy: `serverless package`, prod preview, diff không thuộc loại rủi ro, rồi
   `serverless deploy --package` bằng role OIDC `production` (02-research 4.4.3).
6. E theo dõi metric để xác nhận.
- **Thời gian (quyết định sửa → áp dụng):** ~11–46 phút ⚠️ = PR 2–3 + checks 5–15 + chờ duyệt 0–15 (S7) + package và
  prod preview 1–3 + CloudFormation 3–10. Nếu phải sửa bản fix sau khi đã duyệt thì cộng thêm một vòng duyệt.
- **Còn lại:** không drift, không cần PR codify; bằng chứng nằm sẵn trong PR, run và CloudTrail.

### B — Runbook (SSM Automation)

### A + D2 / A + D2' (để đối chiếu)

- **A + D2 (đọc "JIT cho sự cố"):**
  - Agent read-only đề xuất hai lệnh (Lambda và SQS VT); E xin JIT; R duyệt yêu cầu; E **tự gõ** lệnh trong terminal riêng.
  - CloudTrail ghi E, **giống hệt C**: ở C agent cũng chạy bằng identity của E (02-research 2.9 #1). Khác biệt duy
    nhất là bảo đảm bằng quy trình rằng E đã đọc từng lệnh.
  - Thu hồi có cùng điểm yếu với C. Còn lại: drift trên function và queue, PR codify. Thời gian ~2–20 phút cộng provisioning ⚠️.
- **A + D2':**
  - Thay đổi này **là** IaC, nên đi đường A ở trên (~11–46 phút ⚠️). R sẽ từ chối một yêu cầu JIT cho thay đổi này.
  - Nếu GitHub Actions đang ngừng: yêu cầu JIT liệt kê đúng hai lệnh (`update-function-configuration` và
    `set-queue-attributes` cho VT); R duyệt danh sách đó. Nếu danh sách thiếu lệnh VT, R là người bắt lỗi. Sau đó E
    gõ; job đối chiếu CloudTrail chạy sau cửa sổ; PR codify được mở ngay khi GitHub hoạt động lại; drift detection
    theo dõi cả function lẫn queue tới khi PR merge.

---

## 9. Quyết định của owner

Câu hỏi cần owner trả lời:
- **Q1.** Chọn phương án/tổ hợp nào? (Đề xuất: A + D2', kèm kiểm chứng B ở giai đoạn đầu.) Câu hỏi này cũng là xác
  nhận cách đọc D2: "JIT cho sự cố" hay "IaC trước" (mục 4b).
- **Q2.** Có chấp nhận rằng đường dự phòng JIT chỉ đạt ràng buộc "duyệt thay đổi" **một phần** (5.1) không, với điều
  kiện tần suất được đo và lệch được phát hiện sau?
- **Q3.** Mục tiêu end-to-end cho thay đổi trong sự cố, từ lúc quyết định sửa tới lúc áp dụng? (Đề xuất ⚠️: ≤ 30
  phút, đo ở rollout.)

### Trả lời của owner (2026-11-09)

- **Q1 → A + D2'.** Lý do của owner: cân bằng giữa quy trình và tốc độ xử lý sự cố. Đồng thời chốt cách đọc D2 là
  **"IaC trước"**: JIT không phải đường mặc định cho sự cố.
- **Q2 → Chấp nhận.** Khi có sự cố mà đường chính (A) không dùng được, JIT được dùng sau khi được approve. Owner chấp
  nhận rằng đường này chỉ đạt ràng buộc "duyệt thay đổi" một phần (5.1).
- **Q3 → ≤ 30 phút** từ lúc quyết định sửa tới lúc áp dụng, đo ở rollout.

**Hệ quả cần mang sang bước framework** (ghi chú của agent, không phải lý do của owner):
- Cận trên ước lượng của A trong sự cố (~46 phút ⚠️, mục 6) vượt mục tiêu 30 phút. Đo làn sự cố A trên một service
  thật là việc đầu tiên của rollout. Nếu không đạt, làm A nhanh hơn trước, chứ không nới JIT (mục 7).
- Kiểm chứng B (mục 8) vẫn ở giai đoạn đầu, vì kết quả có thể thu hẹp thêm đường JIT.
- Metric và ngưỡng xem lại cho việc dùng JIT (mục 7) trở thành một phần của bằng chứng cho Q2.
